_purpose: Rules consumed by Module 110 (the light verifier). All three checks (length / format / refusal_sniff) are config-driven so adding a new file format or a new refusal phrase is a one-line edit — no Python change. Phase 14 will add an LLM-judge block here; keep the namespace tidy.

length_check._doc: Compares the requested word count (parsed from the user goal) against the actual word count in the produced docx/chat body. Range allows reasonable over- and under-shoot but flags egregious mismatches (e.g. user asked 500 words, planner shipped 30).

format_check._doc: When the user prompt indicates a file extension OR a tool naturally produces one, verify that an artifact of that extension was actually written and is non-empty. The regex map associates an extension key with patterns we look for in the user's goal; if matched and the resulting affected_resources don't include such a file, the check fails.

refusal_sniff._doc: If the chat.answer body looks like a refusal AND the governance route was BLUE or GREEN (i.e. governance APPROVED the work), that's a soft failure: the agent is refusing despite being allowed. RED / INFEASIBLE routes are exempt because a refusal is the correct response there.

artifact_failure_sniff._doc: P0.2 — a generated office artifact must never contain internal generation-failure / apology text. The judge sees the file, not the reason, so an apology baked into a .docx is a verify-FAIL, not a green VERIFIED. Config-driven phrases; one-line edits.
phrases: 请稍等片刻再让我重做

llm_judge._doc: Phase 14 — LLM-as-judge upgrade. Runs AFTER the three mechanical checks. Cheap mechanical pass-or-skip gates the expensive LLM call: judge only fires when (a) light checks pass AND (b) the task category is in judge_enabled_categories OR judge_enabled_categories is empty (= on for all). Per-rubric pass thresholds live in judge_rubrics.json.

self_fix._doc: Phase 14 — self-fix loop. When the LLM judge fails, runtime re-runs the planner with the judge's feedback in the brief. Capped to bound cost. Each retry is a full pipeline run; the final outcome (pass/fail) is whichever retry the judge accepts (or the last attempt if all fail).

scenario_checks._doc: Phase B — scenario-specific quality rules. The runtime passes pre.task_category into verify(); matching rules from `by_category` are applied as additional sub-checks. Each sub-rule emits its own entry in verification.checks.

_skill_adapted_strict_mode._doc: Phase 2 (L4.6) — when a task was solved using a CROSS-CONTEXT ADAPTED skill (the synthesizer rewrote a stored procedure from one tool to another), the output is held to a stricter bar. (a) extra_min_word_count_pct raises the length_check lower bound so an adapted procedure can't ship a thin artifact; (b) require_target_tool_format_match makes a target-tool-shaped artifact MANDATORY even when the user prompt never named an extension — proof that the adaptation actually produced the new medium. A failure here flows into the same fail_outcome as any other check, and (L4.7) the runtime will NOT credit skill_usage_success for an adapted skill whose task failed verification.

capability_boundary._doc: Q4 §F1 — when the user asks whether the agent can control their computer / desktop, the answer must EXPLAIN capability + governance. Forbid graceful_fallback / 'service busy' style answers — those are correct for API failures, NOT for legitimate boundary questions. The Q3 direct path normally guarantees a good answer; this verifier rule is the safety net for any phrasing the direct path missed.

forbid_phrases.label: no_graceful_fallback_misuse
phrases: couldn't complete that request this time
please wait a moment and send it again
可能是网络或服务暂时繁忙

office_doc_generation._doc: B1 §6 — Word / PowerPoint / Excel direct generation. The light length_check + format_check already verify file existence and word-count when the user asked for a specific length. These scenario sub-rules add: no placeholder text (multi-language), pptx deck has >= 3 slides, xlsx has >= 5 data rows. Bare 'placeholder' was dropped 2026-08-18 — it's a substring match with no word-boundary/context awareness, so it false-positived on an honest sentence like 'contains TBC placeholders' describing the draft's own unfilled fields. The remaining entries (lorem ipsum, fill in here, <content here>, …) are unambiguous unfilled-template tells that never appear in genuine prose.

report_generation._doc: Same rules as office_doc_generation — a 'report' task and an 'office_doc' task both produce a file via docx/pptx/xlsx; the distinction lives only in the classifier keywords. Bare 'placeholder' dropped 2026-08-18 (see office_doc_generation._doc for why).

patent_legal_draft._doc: B3 §8 — patent / legal draft scenario. The agent is drafting a document for a licensed attorney to review. The verifier enforces: (a) an explicit Assumptions section so a reviewer can audit what the AI assumed, (b) a Disclaimer block stating this is NOT legal advice, (c) no lawyer-opinion language like 'we recommend you sue' / '作为律师', (d) a substantive minimum length.

research_report._doc: B2 §7 — web-search-grounded research output. The user said 'search and summarize / 搜索…总结' so the answer MUST cite sources. Sub-rules: a 'Sources:' (or 来源/参考资料/参考) section is present; at least one inline citation marker [1]/[2]/[3]…; the body is substantive (min_word_count); no placeholder text; no graceful_fallback apology body (that's correct for API failures BUT a research task should produce a real cited answer from the hits we already paid for — see 102R R3 web-grounded recovery).
